sentence: This project studies how different rules for keeping schools open affect infection spread, using school and community testing data and model simulations.
This project tries to find out how communities of microbes form, change over time, and stay stable in their host.
This project builds imaging tools that follow scans of the same people over time to detect the effects of Alzheimer's Disease more accurately.
This project coordinates a research center that works to improve understanding of cancer immunology and to develop immunotherapeutic approaches.
This project supports research on the neuroscience behind normal communication and the effects of hearing loss, aiming toward safe and effective therapies.
This project tests synthetic hormones called progestins in women with endometrial cancer to find ones that work well and are safer.
This project studies how virus genomes get trapped in spores of bacteria, how this changes spore development, and how viruses resume infection afterward.
This project builds computer models that link how cells behave to how infection plays out in a whole individual, using deep learning.
This project tests whether a type of MRI scan can detect active tumor growth in patients with an aggressive brain tumor called glioblastoma.
This project builds virus-based vectors that carry genes into skeletal and cardiac muscles to treat genetic muscular diseases such as Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
This project supports a conference where scientists share and discuss the latest discoveries in fungal biology.
This project tries to find out how different types of nerves in the intestine become specialized and how to make specific types of neurons.
This project provides screening of drug libraries and animal studies to help find and develop drugs against cancer.
This project studies how conditions inside diseased cells change the structure and activity of fatty acid synthase, an enzyme that controls fatty acid balance.
This project uses stable isotope labeling and mass spectrometry to study how proteins are made and broken down as stem cells become other cell types.
This project studies the cellular and molecular pathways behind major depressive disorder by looking at gene activity in individual cells.
This project looks for small molecules that could treat spinocerebellar ataxia type 48, which is caused by mutations in a protein with neuroprotective properties.
This project develops ways for doctors and patients with rare genetic disorders to communicate that can improve care.
This project tests a strategy using antisense oligonucleotides to boost the immune response of host cells against tuberculosis.
This project studies how nucleosomes at gene starting points control the start of gene transcription in yeast, using biochemical and structural approaches.
